sections.value:
PASS-WITH-NOTES at eebc7023719fcdf1df3edc8cd14e83955fb9a5bb, final round under C34.

B322-01 and B322-02 are closed:
- The final ledger writer now refuses an empty sender. The original real-store
  generic enqueue({}) -> claim -> ack witness produces an explicit error,
  leaves the claim RUNNING, writes ZERO new wildcard rows, and queues the named
  sender's same-ID message independently. Fake ACK preserves the running claim
  too. Removing the writer guard restores the NEW '' row and AlreadyDelivered
  collapse, killing the original oracle.
- A fully real registry/queue/spine control witness now treats self and parent
  same-ID controls independently: self's refusal is durable; parent queues and
  executes its own control; self's later retry still returns its own refusal.
  Mutants ignoring sender, omitting the scoped record, and dropping the legacy
  brake each fail their intended oracle. Delimiter/UTF-8 key controls pass.
Sources: store/queue.rs:1837-1887,1949-1960; testkit/fakes.rs:1561-1575;
daemon/delivery/mod.rs:1093-1142,2770-2815,3175-3184.

The RUNNING claim question is not universally bounded:
Refusing ACK rolls back the transaction; it adds no timer, retry task or
automatic quarantine. While the invalid claim is RUNNING it blocks only that
serial key, not other recipients. Ordinary Queue::claim, used by native/manual
Copilot reads and generic readers, releases an expired BODY claim back to pending.
It has no three-expiry lifetime budget. A real-store control forced FOUR expired
ordinary leases: the same row was claimed again each time, remained RUNNING with
attempt=4 and lease_expirations=0, while another serial key progressed. The ACK
error is visible; the row's running state and original payload remain inspectable.
An explicit terminal plain ACK freed it, and the queued named-sender message
then claimed and delivered. Plain terminalization writes no delivery ledger row.

This differs from OMP/Pi's claim_extension path, which has the three-expiry
budget and a Working brake, and from expired control claims, which fail rather
than replay. The native ordinary claim lease is300s; the existing <=15s empty-wait
backstop is not a lifetime retry cap.
Normal producer paths I traced still use guarded delivery constructors and named
senders; the production generic enqueue sites are sidecar/remote-send jobs.
No new caller-facing normal delivery route to a senderless job was demonstrated.
Generic/legacy/corrupt direct rows remain a meaningful operational limit.
Sources: queue.rs:109-237,747-766; delivery/mod.rs:2290-2339,2370-2402;
pointer/worker.rs:289-302; http/mod.rs:5510-5564,5623-5657.

new (C34 follow-up) N322-R2-01:
Name an invalid senderless native/ordinary claim's quarantine or terminal-cleanup
policy, or provide explicit operator diagnosis/repair; do not call the job's
lifetime bounded because one claim lease is bounded. This is not a new retry
scheduler or a newly exposed ingress, and does not reopen the final-writer fix.

Legacy refusal / identity answers:
- New product refusals write BOTH the scoped delivery.control-refused record
  and a delivery.outcome with from present, before the queue ACK. The scoped
  key uses the sender's UTF-8 byte length and its exact id; another sender/id
  pair cannot substitute a delimiter boundary.
- The match-any legacy brake is specifically absent/null from on an old-shaped
  control refusal, not every fallback read. The code also permits a fallback
  NEW refusal from the SAME sender; that is ordinary own-sender replay, not
  match-any legacy replay. A generated new refusal from another sender cannot
  take that branch. Legacy behavior is identified by payload shape, not a
  migration-date predicate; all new product refusal writers supply from.
- The dedicated scoped record is necessary: another sender's later outcome can
  overwrite the latest unscoped outcome for the raw id. The missing-record
  mutant then requeues self's previously refused control, and our real-store
  witness catches it.
- C33/raw-body sender assertion remains the stated inherited limit. Control
  admission still derives its actor through the existing control authorization;
  this PR does not grant a new caller identity or execution permission.

Migration / cost / merge:
Migration0050 is byte-for-byte unchanged from round1. Its row-preservation and
legacy-row retry test passes again; the independent mid-migration-error rollback
and two-open idempotence control passes at R2 too. The final merge is clean and
the freeze still checks0050 above main's0049.
No new periodic timer, process launch or retry job. Each control admission adds
the scoped refusal read plus fallback when absent; each is a schema read and
seat/kind JSON-key search, not an O(1) message index guarantee. Each terminal
refusal also writes the extra scoped event. A stuck ordinary body claim can
recycle at existing claim opportunities; that is covered by the note above.
The PR now distinguishes point-key pairs, payload parsing, settlement history
and snapshot index sizes. Release store-open0.796/0.576s figures remain the
performance receipt from prior head c0cae51, not a fresh R2 full-bounce benchmark.

Validation:
- Exact-head session archive, real SQLite and fake tmux, no source edits to the
  review checkout. Shared target/nice19/four jobs: message_sender3/3, queue50/50,
  independent store controls7/7, real control/key controls3/3; total63 positives.
- Four/four source mutants killed: final writer without sender guard, refusal
  sender ignored, scoped refusal not written, legacy brake removed. Mutation
  batch exit101 is expected; no positive-control failure.
- Production macOS clippy -Dwarnings for daemon/store/testkit libs: exit0.
- CI44922138243, successful rust-testjob136900289680, successful artifact
  14714272344: independently parsed2,827 cases, zero failures; original sender,
  migration, held-expiry and new/legacy control cases passed.
- harness checks --quick: exit1, eight dependency/ambient-tool failures;
  native contracts, SDK and pij-skill passed; heavy stages skipped. No C25
  dependency links or repeated unbounded workspace suite. No full local green.
- just pr-freeze322: final publication is bound to this exact head, CI5/5,
  CLEAN, migration50 over49. No production DB write, working-seat spawn or bounce.

Harness lesson: refusal at the final writer protects identity, but is not a
terminal row policy. Test ACK atomicity, claim recovery, queue progress and
sender-scoped negative replay as separate proof obligations.
